Redis on ElastiCache Serverless, function roles that stop trusting your whole AWS account outside `sst dev`, and fixes for `sst dev` and `sst tunnel`. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **The role SST creates for a function now trusts only Lambda, except in `sst dev`.** Before, every function role also trusted your AWS account, so anyone in it who is allowed to assume roles could take on a deployed function's permissions. The first `sst deploy` after you update changes each function role in place, so a deploy role with limited permissions needs `iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy`. `sst dev` on a deployed stage adds the account back until the next deploy. If something assumes a deployed function's role on purpose, add the trust back with `transform.role`. ([#95](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/95), [anomalyco/sst#7026](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/7026))

### New

- **`sst.aws.Redis` can create an ElastiCache Serverless cache**, with `serverless: true` or with `storage` and `ecpuPerSecond` limits. It links `host`, `port`, `username` and a generated `password` like a provisioned cluster, and `serverless: { password: false }` leaves the password out. A deploy role with limited permissions needs the ElastiCache user and user group actions in the [`password` docs](https://sst-community.github.io/sst/docs/component/aws/redis#serverless-password). Turning `serverless` on or off for an existing Redis replaces the cache, and its data is lost. ([#91](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/91), [anomalyco/sst#6219](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6219))

### Fixes

- **A killed `sst tunnel` or `sst dev` no longer leaves the tunnel running**, which blocked the next one with "Another tunnel process is already running". The fix is in the copy at `/opt/sst/tunnel`, so run `sudo sst tunnel install` again after you update. Run it outside a project folder: inside one, it installs the `sst` in that project's `node_modules`. ([#101](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/101), [anomalyco/sst#6297](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6297))
- **`sst dev` no longer hangs when a function's response is lost on the way back** after a cold start. The response is sent again a few times. ([#102](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/102), [anomalyco/sst#6575](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6575))
- **`sst dev` keeps a function's build output while it rebuilds**, so a running function no longer loses its `bundle.mjs`. ([#100](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/100), [anomalyco/sst#6416](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6416))
- **`sst dev` no longer grows in memory as it builds functions.** It keeps at most 4 esbuild build contexts. `SST_BUILD_CONTEXT_CACHE` changes that; keep it at or above `SST_BUILD_CONCURRENCY_FUNCTION`. ([#90](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/90), [anomalyco/sst#6960](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6960))
- **Functions that share a `bundle` directory each get their own links.** Each has its own `.sst/<function name>/resource.enc` there, and its zip carries only that one. A `.sst` folder you keep in a bundle directory is no longer uploaded. ([#89](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/89), [anomalyco/sst#6772](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6772))

### Also

- The README has Discord, npm and build badges. The automatic review works with its free model again ([#93](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/93)).

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.0
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.0"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
